---
title: "Final project"
subtitle: "A reproducible research pipeline"
---

Bring the course practices together in a project whose evidence another person can inspect. Use a common template and a guided agent workflow, adapted to a research question approved by the responsible human.

## Pipeline

| Stage | Expected record |
|---|---|
| Data sourcing | Source manifest, access conditions, and preserved inputs |
| Question management | Research question, authority boundaries, and decision record |
| Merging | Approved matching rules and checks of matched and unmatched records |
| Analysis | Approved specification, reproducible commands, and checked outputs |
| Visualization | Figures traceable to analysis results and appropriately qualified labels |
| Website presentation | A clear account of the method, evidence, uncertainty, and limitations |

## Submission package

- A task brief and human-approved substantive decisions.
- Scripts, environment information, and commands that reproduce the work.
- Source and execution records, verification evidence, and unresolved questions.
- A website explaining the findings without overstating what the evidence establishes.
- A handoff that makes continuation possible.

A bounded version of a larger research task may be appropriate. The final scope, workload, and rubric will be set with the instructor.

## Research-assistant applications

Students interested in the lab may use the project as part of a research-assistant application. Project completion is evidence of work for review; it does not guarantee an appointment.

## Data and publication

Use only data and code permitted by the project's access and reuse conditions. Share links or a reproducible retrieval procedure when redistributing inputs is not allowed. Author contact, third-party code execution, purchases, and publication retain their own approval requirements.
